name: Pregnenolone

lead: Pregnenolone is made from cholesterol and sits at the start of the steroid pathway, leading to progesterone, cortisol, DHEA, testosterone and estrogens. It is also made in the brain. Users take it for hormone support, mood and libido, hoping that supporting hormones helps muscle and leanness.

On forums it is discussed through the 'pregnenolone steal' idea, that stress diverts it toward cortisol. Controlled trials of oral pregnenolone have been in psychiatry, such as bipolar depression and schizophrenia; none found tested testosterone, physique or appearance.

paras: It is taken as a daily supplement capsule, often alongside DHEA, as part of a hormone-support routine. Users mostly judge mood, libido and energy.

Because it feeds several hormone pathways, effects can be unpredictable, and a forum poster advises supervision. It is sold as a US supplement with limited regulatory evaluation; long-term data in healthy users are lacking.

social.title: Scientist thinks hormone pregnenolone might reduce lonely people’s fear

angle.text: Pregnenolone is the precursor to testosterone, cortisol and DHEA, and users take it to support hormone levels and, through them, muscle and leanness. Trials exist for mood and psychiatric uses; a testosterone or appearance effect from supplementing has not been tested.

lead: Pregnenolone is a steroid made from cholesterol that serves as the biosynthetic precursor of other steroid hormones, including progesterone, cortisol, DHEA, testosterone and estrogens [1][2]. It is produced in the adrenal glands, gonads and brain, and is also classed as a neurosteroid [3][4]. It is sold as an over-the-counter dietary supplement in the United States [5].

In looksmaxxing and testosterone-optimisation circles it is taken or discussed as hormone support, often alongside DHEA or testosterone replacement therapy, with the aim of better mood, energy, libido and body composition, which people connect to looking fitter and healthier. It also features in the idea of "pregnenolone steal", the claim that stress and stimulants divert pregnenolone away from sex-hormone production toward cortisol [6][7]. The Ray Peat-influenced community, which discusses pregnenolone alongside progesterone and DHEA, is one source of this interest [8].

Published trials of oral pregnenolone have been conducted mainly in psychiatry, including bipolar depression, schizophrenia, autism and substance use disorders [9][10][11]. A pharmacokinetic summary on Wikipedia reports that oral pregnenolone has low bioavailability and extensive metabolism, and that small oral doses produced minimal change in urinary testosterone while raising urinary pregnanediol and pregnanolone [5]. No trial found has tested it for testosterone levels, physique or appearance outcomes.
infobox: Cholesterol, in adrenals, gonads and brain [4][2][18]
Negative allosteric modulator of CB1; PXR agonist [18]
Sold as a dietary supplement in the US; availability varies elsewhere [5]

paras: Pregnenolone is formed when the enzyme CYP11A1 cleaves the side chain of cholesterol inside mitochondria, a rate-limiting step regulated by the steroidogenic acute regulatory protein [12][1]. From pregnenolone, downstream enzymes lead to progesterone, mineralocorticoids, glucocorticoids and sex steroids [1][2]. Leydig cells in the testis perform this conversion for testosterone production [13]. Pregnenolone is also made in the brain, where research in animals has linked it to neurosteroid activity and, in one mouse study, recognition memory [3][14]. In rat hippocampal tissue, neurons were found to make estradiol from pregnenolone [15]. Pregnenolone and related pregnanes also activate the pregnane X receptor, a nuclear receptor that induces drug-metabolising enzymes [16][17].

Wikipedia gives typical circulating levels as roughly 10 to 200 ng/dL in men and notes that castration does not significantly change them in men, consistent with a mainly adrenal source [18]. It is lipophilic and crosses the blood-brain barrier, while its sulfate form does not [18]. Enzymes convert it along two routes: 3-beta-hydroxysteroid dehydrogenase leads to progesterone and then on to testosterone, cortisol and aldosterone, while CYP17A1 leads to 17-hydroxypregnenolone and DHEA [18]. Wikipedia states that pregnenolone itself has no androgenic, estrogenic, progestogenic or glucocorticoid activity [18].

Pregnenolone sulfate negatively modulates GABA-A receptors and positively modulates NMDA receptors, and neurosteroids in general are linked in the literature to synaptic function, neuroprotection and myelination [18]. Pregnenolone also binds microtubule-associated protein 2 and acts as a negative allosteric modulator of the cannabinoid CB1 receptor; a 2014 Science study cited by Wikipedia reported that it may protect the brain from the effects of cannabis intoxication [18].

Wikipedia summarises that oral pregnenolone has low bioavailability and extensive metabolism. In the studies it cites, oral doses had minimal effect on urinary testosterone and its metabolites, but clearly raised urinary pregnanediol and pregnanolone; a single larger oral dose raised blood pregnenolone about threefold and allopregnanolone about sevenfold at 3 hours, with DHEA and cortisol unchanged [5]. For comparison, the same article says only about 1.5 percent of an oral DHEA dose is converted to testosterone [5].

Adolf Butenandt and colleagues first synthesized pregnenolone in 1934, and it entered medicine as an anti-inflammatory in the 1940s [18][5]. The branded product Enelone, containing pregnenolone acetate, was approved in the 1950s for rheumatoid arthritis and soft-tissue rheumatism by oral, topical and injected routes, and pregnenolone is no longer marketed as a prescription medicine [5]. A 1950 clinical article is among the earliest in the medical literature [19]. The discovery of the StAR protein in 1995 clarified how cholesterol reaches the enzyme that makes pregnenolone [12]. Wikipedia lists past brand names including Enelone, Natolone, Regnosone and Sharmone [5].

On looksmax.org, an original post describes pregnenolone as the base of the steroid pathway and recommends supplementing it for broad benefits [4]. Another thread argues that caffeine and stimulants lower testosterone through "pregnenolone steal" [6], and a third relays advice from the Ray Peat-influenced community to combine pregnenolone with other drugs for stress and attention problems [8]. On T Nation, users on TRT report adding pregnenolone with DHEA, or take it for anxiety, mood, libido and water retention [20][21][22][23]. Other posters dispute its value, saying that people who eat adequate cholesterol should not need it [24], and one user reports no noticeable effect from cream or pills [25].

A randomized placebo-controlled trial in 80 adults with bipolar depression tested add-on pregnenolone for 12 weeks [9]. Further trials and registrations have examined it in schizophrenia [10][26], autism [27][28], depression with substance use [29], alcohol or cannabis use disorders [30][31], PTSD [32] and perceived social isolation [33]. The studies are psychiatric and clinical, and none concerns healthy men seeking testosterone or physique effects. A 1950 clinical article is among the earliest in the medical literature [19].

Wikipedia notes that as of 2016 pregnenolone was under study for therapeutic uses but that poor bioavailability was described as limiting prospects, and that a derivative, 3-beta-methoxypregnenolone (MAP-4343), is in development for brain and spinal cord injury and depressive disorders [5]. In a 2025 pilot randomised trial in 55 adults with cocaine use disorder, pregnenolone groups had higher pregnenolone levels and did not show the rise in stress- and cue-induced craving seen in the placebo group, while the reduction in percent days of cocaine use was not statistically significant [11]. A 2026 randomised trial in 60 adults with alcohol use disorder examined stress- and cue-provoked pain and reported differences between dose groups [11]. These studies concern addiction and psychiatric outcomes rather than testosterone or appearance.

A US-listed homeopathic oral product that includes pregnenolone alongside DHEA, estradiol, progesterone and testosterone carries the statement that its claims are based on traditional homeopathic practice and that it is not FDA evaluated [34]. Hormone precursors in the body are converted to downstream steroids in ways that vary between individuals, and a clinician-supervised approach is advised in one forum post [35]; published trials in healthy users are lacking.

Wikipedia reports that pregnenolone remains an over-the-counter supplement in the United States, and that online promotion has claimed benefits for cancer, arthritis and multiple sclerosis which the American Cancer Society, as cited there, states are unsupported [5]. The article has no adverse-effects section; as a precursor, its metabolites include other neuroactive steroids, and people on testosterone therapy discuss monitoring hormone levels with their clinician [35][5].

lore.intro: Pregnenolone is described on looksmax.org and T Nation as a master precursor hormone to supplement or protect from being "stolen" by stress [4][6][7].
